bull_bear.body: Free Cash Flow FY26: Rs. 9,200 Cr (Standalone), ~12% of revenue. Dividend: Final dividend of Rs. 4/share recommended (~Rs. 1,500 Cr outflow). Net Cash: Rs. 7,500 Cr (Standalone), Rs. 13,700 Cr (Consolidated). Iveco Deal Financing: Initial bridge loan followed by refinancing; mix of debt/equity to be finalized closer to closure (expected Q2 FY27).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Diesel Price Volatility: Key monitorable impacting TCO and transporter profitability. Commodity Inflation: Severe headwinds in Q1 FY27 affecting margins. Geopolitical: Middle East/North Africa sentiment cautious; shipment delays managed but impact present. Regulatory: Pending financial regulatory approvals for Iveco deal (France, Spain). EV Bus Tender Pricing: Unsustainable quotes in government tenders limiting participation.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident in structural profitability and market share gains but prudently cautious on near-term macro headwinds (diesel, commodities). Emphasizes 'quarter-by-quarter' visibility over full-year guidance due to external uncertainties. Focus on volume protection over aggressive price passing.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Strategic inventory build-up in Q4 due to geopolitical risks distorted working capital flow but was planned. EV bus market participation is being curtailed not due to lack of demand but due to 'unsustainable' competitor pricing in tenders, signaling a potential future consolidation or correction in that sub-segment. Replacement cycle is real for large fleets (40% of volume) but old trucks are often sold down to smaller duty cycles rather than scrapped, keeping total fleet age high.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

- Net cash of ₹7.1K Cr at Jun-26 on the standalone (incl. JO Tata Cummins) basis versus ₹7.5K Cr at Mar-26, after a dividend payment of ₹1.5K Cr.

- Auto ROCE of 68% in Q1 FY27 (FY25 61%, FY26 72%), analytically derived as last-twelve-months EBIT divided by average capital employed (YoY).

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA margin 13.9% despite ~100 bps commodity headwind (steel, aluminum, copper, precious metals). Management implemented a 2% price increase in April but is absorbing remaining inflation to protect demand. Cost levers and operational excellence are key focus areas to maintain 'teens' margin guidance amidst rupee devaluation and input cost spikes.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Single-digit growth expected in Q1 FY27; full year FY27 guidance withheld due to diesel/commodity uncertainty. Margin: Targeting 'teens' (not mid-teens) EBITDA; Q1 expected to face severe commodity headwinds partially offset by 2% price hike and cost levers. Order Inflow: Strong pipeline conversion expected for buses and exports; Indonesia shipments ramping rapidly. Capex/Commissioning: FY27 Capex guided at 2-4% of revenue (similar to FY26's ~Rs. 3,000 Cr); focus on new tech and capacity for EVs/new models.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 70,000 units (Indonesia - Yodha/Ultra T.7, homologation complete, first shipment en route); 5,000 buses (State Transport Undertakings); 250 electric buses (recent orders); 40 H2-ICE trucks (V.O.C Port trial); Robust domestic HCV and SCV pipeline driven by replacement cycle and infrastructure activity.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Indonesia export ramp-up (70k units); EV penetration in SCV segment (targeting high single-digit %); Hydrogen ICE trials (V.O.C Port); Market share gains in HCV replacing aging fleet (40% of volume from large fleet replacements); Micro-segmental strategy driving traction in specific geographies/end-uses.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Building an ecosystem play beyond the vehicle itself — charging infrastructure for electric fleets, financial partnerships to improve fleet-financing access, and collaboration with fuel and logistics partners — positioning the Company as a comprehensive mobility solutions provider rather than simply a vehicle manufacturer.
- Protecting margins under commodity-cost pressure through a combination of selective pricing actions and a focused cost-management programme spanning procurement, manufacturing efficiency and value engineering, calibrated to preserve customer affordability and long-term relationships.
- Resilient business strategy anchored around delivering superior customer economics through product relevance, operating efficiency and lifecycle value creation, underpinned by engineering prowess, on-ground market insight and a strong service network.
- Advancing the Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV) journey from foundational organisational readiness to execution-ready platform development, including vehicle architecture, high-performance computing strategy and a structured software development lifecycle.
- Material technology roadmap balancing short-term lightweighting benefits, medium-term electrification needs and long-term hydrogen and circularity solutions.
- R&D engineering strategy oriented toward enabling global growth through differentiated, locally relevant technology platforms (rather than one-size-fits-all replication), with emphasis on modular design and deeper collaboration with global and local partners.
- Proposed acquisition of Iveco Group's industrial and financial services business as a key strategic development, positioning Tata Motors as a leading global commercial-vehicle manufacturer in the 6-tonne segment and above with a more diversified, globally present entity.
- FY27 priorities: scaling the refreshed product portfolio, sustaining profitable growth across segments, expanding electric and sustainable mobility offerings, growing international business while navigating geopolitical risks, and maintaining cost discipline and capital efficiency.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 saw an expansive product launch calendar spanning the Profit, Safety, Progress and Sustainability series of trucks, the next-generation Tata Trucks.ev electric truck range (7 to 55 tonnes) built on the modular i MoEV architecture, the Azura Series in ILMCV, the Ace Pro last-mile platform (Bi-fuel/EV/Petrol), the Ultra range for intra-city logistics, and Prima vehicles for infrastructure/mining/construction, alongside Euro VI-compliant models and purpose-built solutions for the Middle East, Qatar, Egypt, Sri Lanka, the Dominican Republic and the wider MENA region, supporting market expansion in India and key international markets. On the energy side, the Company continued adding on-site renewable (solar) generation capacity during FY26, taking total installed on-site solar capacity to 59.9 MWp across six sites (Pimpri, Chinchwad, Jamshedpur, Pantnagar, Lucknow and Dharwad), and plans to continue sourcing off-site renewable power via Power Purchase Agreements going forward. The Re.Wi.Re end-of-life-vehicle recycling initiative was expanded through a franchise-based model to a total of 11 facilities with a combined annual dismantling capacity exceeding 190,000 vehicles, and the Company stated it remains committed to further expanding this network across the country. Separately, the Company reported that 33% of its total R&D expenditure and 28% of its total Capex in FY26 were directed toward specific technologies aimed at improving the environmental and social impact of products and processes, assessed against European Sustainability Taxonomy criteria.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Industry growth is expected to be more moderate in FY27 than FY26, reflecting a higher base and near-term uncertainties in the external environment.
- Underlying demand drivers for commercial vehicles in India remain constructive, supported by infrastructure activity, improving fleet utilisation and the ongoing transition toward cleaner and more connected transport.
- India's real GDP grew 7.6% in FY26 on resilient consumption and steady investment momentum; IMF expects FY27 GDP growth of 6.5%, reaffirming confidence in India's long-term structural growth drivers.
- Union Budget FY27 proposed a capital expenditure outlay of Rs 12.22 lakh crore, up from Rs 11.21 lakh crore in FY26, expected to support construction, mining and logistics activity and directly benefit core CV segments.
- The CV industry recorded its highest-ever annual volumes of 10.79 lakh units in FY26, up 12.6% year-on-year and surpassing the earlier FY19 peak, with a sharp second-half rebound after a soft first half.
- Demand recovery in the second half was enabled by GST 2.0 rollout, RBI repo rate cuts, firmer freight rates, higher e-commerce-led logistics movement, renewed infrastructure activity and improved financing conditions (better returns, lower NPAs).
- Consistent growth in e-way bill generation reflected underlying health of goods movement, reinforcing structural demand for commercial vehicles; fleet operators returned to buying with greater conviction in H2 on stable interest rates, manageable fuel prices and low financing delinquencies.
- Rising commodity costs (steel, aluminium, copper) emerged as a key area of concern into FY27, requiring disciplined cost management and a measured price increase to partially offset pressure while protecting affordability.
- Diesel prices remain a key monitorable given their role in total cost of ownership for fleet operators; a sustained rise could temper industry buying decisions.
- International business was a standout performer, with export volumes posting significant year-on-year growth driven by large international orders and focused market development, though the West Asia conflict began affecting sentiment in North Africa and Middle East export markets.
- Electric commercial vehicles continued to gain traction, led by buses and small commercial vehicles, driven by improving total-cost-of-ownership economics and supportive government policies.
- FY27 headwinds flagged include commodity cost pressure, geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia developments) and potential demand implications of new regulatory requirements.
- International business growth was driven in part by large international orders and focused market development efforts, though no specific backlog or order-book figure was disclosed.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Tata Motors has successfully transitioned to a pure-play CV entity with record profitability (13.2% FY26 EBITDA) driven by premiumization and operating leverage, though FY27 faces near-term margin pressure from commodity inflation and diesel price volatility which management is absorbing to protect volume momentum. The massive 70k unit Indonesia order and strong domestic replacement cycle provide visibility, but guidance is now quarter-by-quarter due to external macro uncertainties.

open.item: Board of Directors recommended a final dividend of Rs 4 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.

Company's stated FY27 priorities are scaling the refreshed product portfolio, sustaining profitable growth across segments, expanding electric and sustainable mobility offerings, growing international business while navigating geopolitical risks, and maintaining cost discipline and capital efficiency.

Company announced the proposed acquisition of the IVECO Group, adding a light/medium/heavy CV portfolio across European, Latin American and other international markets with annual sales of approximately 140,000 vehicles and 2025 revenues of EUR13.4 billion.
Company is progressing toward 100% renewable electricity across its operations.
While scaling the portfolio of zero-emission electric CVs, the Company will continue to invest in hydrogen-based technologies for heavier-duty commercial vehicle segments.

Proposed acquisition of Iveco Group's industrial and financial services business is intended to position Tata Motors as a leading global CV manufacturer in the 6-tonne segment and above, creating a stronger, more diversified entity with significant global presence.

Multiple technology-absorption projects remain under development, including a fuel-agnostic engine, diesel-engine blend development, fusion-based ADAS systems, and a Virtual Test Bed for gasoline engines (imported FY26).
Company progressed its hydrogen roadmap with pilot deployments of hydrogen-powered trucks underway on select freight corridors, as part of its ongoing alternate-fuel agenda.

Company plans to continue sourcing off-site renewable power via Power Purchase Agreements, in line with regulatory policies/frameworks and tariffs in the states where it operates, to continue offsetting greenhouse gas emissions in coming years.

Company remains committed to further expanding its Re.Wi.Re vehicle-dismantling franchise network across the country, beyond the current 11 facilities with combined annual dismantling capacity exceeding 190,000 vehicles.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited) is India's undisputed leader in the Commercial Vehicles market, operating since November 2025 as a standalone listed CV-only entity following its demerger from erstwhile Tata Motors Limited.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures, sells, markets and provides customer support for commercial vehicles and spare parts across India and 45+ international markets. Its customer base spans fleet owners, transporters, government agencies, defense, public transport utilities, SMEs, and the agriculture/rural, mining and construction sectors, organised internally into an eight-vertical structure covering four vehicular segments (Heavy Commercial Vehicles, Intermediate Light & Medium Commercial Vehicles, Small Commercial Vehicles & Pickups, and electric buses via TML Smart City Mobility Solutions) plus non-cyclical spares/services, digital platforms and international business.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Industry growth is expected to be more moderate in FY27 than FY26, reflecting a higher base and near-term uncertainties in the external environment.
- Underlying demand drivers for commercial vehicles in India remain constructive, supported by infrastructure activity, improving fleet utilisation and the ongoing transition toward cleaner and more connected transport.
- India's real GDP grew 7.6% in FY26 on resilient consumption and steady investment momentum; IMF expects FY27 GDP growth of 6.5%, reaffirming confidence in India's long-term structural growth drivers.
- Union Budget FY27 proposed a capital expenditure outlay of Rs 12.22 lakh crore, up from Rs 11.21 lakh crore in FY26, expected to support construction, mining and logistics activity and directly benefit core CV segments.
- The CV industry recorded its highest-ever annual volumes of 10.79 lakh units in FY26, up 12.6% year-on-year and surpassing the earlier FY19 peak, with a sharp second-half rebound after a soft first half.
- Demand recovery in the second half was enabled by GST 2.0 rollout, RBI repo rate cuts, firmer freight rates, higher e-commerce-led logistics movement, renewed infrastructure activity and improved financing conditions (better returns, lower NPAs).
- Consistent growth in e-way bill generation reflected underlying health of goods movement, reinforcing structural demand for commercial vehicles; fleet operators returned to buying with greater conviction in H2 on stable interest rates, manageable fuel prices and low financing delinquencies.
- Rising commodity costs (steel, aluminium, copper) emerged as a key area of concern into FY27, requiring disciplined cost management and a measured price increase to partially offset pressure while protecting affordability.
- Diesel prices remain a key monitorable given their role in total cost of ownership for fleet operators; a sustained rise could temper industry buying decisions.
- International business was a standout performer, with export volumes posting significant year-on-year growth driven by large international orders and focused market development, though the West Asia conflict began affecting sentiment in North Africa and Middle East export markets.
- Electric commercial vehicles continued to gain traction, led by buses and small commercial vehicles, driven by improving total-cost-of-ownership economics and supportive government policies.
- FY27 headwinds flagged include commodity cost pressure, geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia developments) and potential demand implications of new regulatory requirements.
- International business growth was driven in part by large international orders and focused market development efforts, though no specific backlog or order-book figure was disclosed.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA margin 13.9% despite ~100 bps commodity headwind (steel, aluminum, copper, precious metals). Management implemented a 2% price increase in April but is absorbing remaining inflation to protect demand. Cost levers and operational excellence are key focus areas to maintain 'teens' margin guidance amidst rupee devaluation and input cost spikes.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Free Cash Flow FY26: Rs. 9,200 Cr (Standalone), ~12% of revenue. Dividend: Final dividend of Rs. 4/share recommended (~Rs. 1,500 Cr outflow). Net Cash: Rs. 7,500 Cr (Standalone), Rs. 13,700 Cr (Consolidated). Iveco Deal Financing: Initial bridge loan followed by refinancing; mix of debt/equity to be finalized closer to closure (expected Q2 FY27).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 saw an expansive product launch calendar spanning the Profit, Safety, Progress and Sustainability series of trucks, the next-generation Tata Trucks.ev electric truck range (7 to 55 tonnes) built on the modular i MoEV architecture, the Azura Series in ILMCV, the Ace Pro last-mile platform (Bi-fuel/EV/Petrol), the Ultra range for intra-city logistics, and Prima vehicles for infrastructure/mining/construction, alongside Euro VI-compliant models and purpose-built solutions for the Middle East, Qatar, Egypt, Sri Lanka, the Dominican Republic and the wider MENA region, supporting market expansion in India and key international markets. On the energy side, the Company continued adding on-site renewable (solar) generation capacity during FY26, taking total installed on-site solar capacity to 59.9 MWp across six sites (Pimpri, Chinchwad, Jamshedpur, Pantnagar, Lucknow and Dharwad), and plans to continue sourcing off-site renewable power via Power Purchase Agreements going forward. The Re.Wi.Re end-of-life-vehicle recycling initiative was expanded through a franchise-based model to a total of 11 facilities with a combined annual dismantling capacity exceeding 190,000 vehicles, and the Company stated it remains committed to further expanding this network across the country. Separately, the Company reported that 33% of its total R&D expenditure and 28% of its total Capex in FY26 were directed toward specific technologies aimed at improving the environmental and social impact of products and processes, assessed against European Sustainability Taxonomy criteria.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident in structural profitability and market share gains but prudently cautious on near-term macro headwinds (diesel, commodities). Emphasizes 'quarter-by-quarter' visibility over full-year guidance due to external uncertainties. Focus on volume protection over aggressive price passing.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Undisputed leadership in India's Commercial Vehicles market built on enduring brand strength, people capability and customer trust earned over decades
- HCV Trucks business achieved its strongest offtake market share in a decade (55%), driven by sharper segment strategies and consultative selling
- Fleet Edge connected-vehicle platform crossed one million connected vehicles, strengthening customer engagement and operating-economics insight for consultative selling
- Automotive business delivered return on capital employed of 72.3%, cited as among the highest in the global commercial vehicles industry
- Part of the Tata Group, with Tata Code of Conduct, Tata Business Excellence Model and Balanced Scorecard governance framework underpinning brand and governance credibility

risks.body: Diesel Price Volatility: Key monitorable impacting TCO and transporter profitability. Commodity Inflation: Severe headwinds in Q1 FY27 affecting margins. EV Bus Tender Pricing: Unsustainable quotes in government tenders limiting participation.

non_obvious.body: Strategic inventory build-up in Q4 due to geopolitical risks distorted working capital flow but was planned. EV bus market participation is being curtailed not due to lack of demand but due to 'unsustainable' competitor pricing in tenders, signaling a potential future consolidation or correction in that sub-segment. Replacement cycle is real for large fleets (40% of volume) but old trucks are often sold down to smaller duty cycles rather than scrapped, keeping total fleet age high.

strategy.body:
- Building an ecosystem play beyond the vehicle itself — charging infrastructure for electric fleets, financial partnerships to improve fleet-financing access, and collaboration with fuel and logistics partners — positioning the Company as a comprehensive mobility solutions provider rather than simply a vehicle manufacturer.
- Protecting margins under commodity-cost pressure through a combination of selective pricing actions and a focused cost-management programme spanning procurement, manufacturing efficiency and value engineering, calibrated to preserve customer affordability and long-term …

Replacement cycle is real for large fleets (40% of volume) but old trucks are often sold down to smaller duty cycles rather than scrapped, keeping total fleet age high.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

hero.oneLiner: Tata Motors Limited (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited) is India's undisputed leader in the Commercial Vehicles market, operating since November 2025 as a standalone listed CV-only entity following its demerger from erstwhile Tata Motors Limited.
